text:
oliver: Quick follow-up from the scheduler/queueing sync. I want to discuss trimming vs. compaction and where backlog accounting should live.
mei: I've been leaning toward keeping backlog accounting in the scheduler but letting the batcher perform physical compaction. Scheduler tracks "logical free" and batcher does the heavy I/O.
rachel: Problem we saw: scheduler-only logical frees lead to overcommit when compaction lag grows under heavy GC churn. We need a tighter feedback loop.
sam: Two proposals: (A) fast feedback stream + delayed compaction, (B) reclaim RPC + reserved window. Both have pros.
oliver: Sketch A: batcher emits a compactness score every 150ms: small integer 0..3 where 3 = highly fragmented. Scheduler multiplies that into its admission curve. Minimal surface.
mei: Sketch B: scheduler requests reclaim with a lease token; batcher returns a reserved credit token when compaction finishes. Scheduler redeems the token to admit work. Safer but more RPCs.
rachel: We can hybridize: shaping hint first (ask batcher to coalesce gently), only escalate to reclaim when compactness score stays high for N windows.
sam: Important: add hysteresis and a TTL on reserved tokens to avoid token hoarding. Also idempotency keys for reclaim so retries are safe.
oliver: Wire example (text):
```
GET /batcher/compactness -> {lane, score, head_gap_ms}
POST /batcher/shaping -> {lane, lease_token} => {shaped:true, est_freed:2}
POST /batcher/reclaim -> {lane, lease_token, mode:async} => {job_id}
POST /batcher/reclaim/ack -> {job_id} => {freed_slots, credits_token, reserve_ms}
POST /scheduler/credits/redeem -> {credits_token, amount}
```
mei: Observability: track `compactness.score`, `reclaim.latency`, `credits.redeem.latency`. We need p99 for redeem latency.
rachel: Edge case: lane ownership transfer mid-reclaim. Solution: reclaim must carry ownership version; batcher refuses if mismatch and returns `ownership_conflict:true`. Scheduler then re-evaluates.
sam: Rollout: start with compactness stream + shaping endpoint behind FF. Reclaim remains disabled until we validate shaping reduces p99.
ci-bot: deploy-notice: batcher-shaping-v1 -> canary 5% us-west at 09:00 UTC. Healthchecks 10m.
oliver: Action items: mei -> implement compactness export; rachel -> add shaping handler; sam -> perf harness to simulate ownership transfer. I'll draft RFC with hybrid flow and TTL semantics.
mei: I'll also add a small simulation in the RFC showing token TTL impact on throughput.
rachel: Thanks—will review RFC once you post.
